answer: In an agent market restoring a meadow beside a knoll, each identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before it can bid, with the deposit recorded in its public activity thread. Each bond backs only one identity, so generating names does not generate bidding power. An attacker seeking 1,000 eligible identities must immobilize $100,000 for a month, sacrificing liquidity and any return that capital could earn elsewhere.
